exposure: Nested case-control analysis comparing children who developed islet autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes to those who did not
cohort: 903 children aged 3 to 46 months participating in the The Environmental Determinants of Diabetes in the Young (TEDDY) study
finding: The developing gut microbiome undergoes three distinct phases of progression (developmental, transitional, stable) and is significantly influenced by breastfeeding, birth mode, and environmental factors, with subtle associations also observed between microbial taxonomy and the development of islet autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes.
mod_finding: Birth mode was significantly associated with the gut microbiome during the developmental phase, with infants delivered vaginally having higher levels of Bacteroides species.
